nom: e.l.f. Cosmetics Suntouchable Invisible Sunscreen SPF 35

segments.dry: Dry-skin reviewers are split: several find it comfortable, moisturizing and non-greasy, but one reviewer with dry skin calls it greasy and would never use it on the face.
segments.oily: Oily-skin reviewers mostly report a matte, blurred, non-greasy finish that layers well under makeup, though one reviewer with oily skin found it too thick and gunky and would not recommend it for oily skin.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin, including one prone to allergic reactions from other sunscreens, report no irritation, no eye-watering and no redness with this product.
segments.mature: One reviewer in her 60s (using it after 40 years of avoiding facial sunscreen) reports it is the first that doesn't break her out or feel greasy, with a smoother-looking complexion.

concerns.aging: One long-term user reports smoother-looking complexion and no adverse reaction after decades of avoiding facial sunscreen, though this speaks to tolerability more than to visible aging improvement.
concerns.dehydration: Several reviewers describe it as hydrating, comfortable and non-drying, including on dry skin, with one using it in place of a moisturizer.
concerns.redness: One reviewer reports it is the first sunscreen that hasn't caused redness, swelling, itching or irritation; two fair-skinned/redheaded reviewers report getting sunburned despite use.
concerns.barrier: No reviews specifically discuss barrier repair or damage.
concerns.spots: Two reviewers, including a longtime redhead/ginger, report getting pink or sunburned despite reapplication, attributing it to the SPF 35 being insufficient for their needs.
concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers who mention breakouts report none, including a 40-year sunscreen-avoider and daily users; one reviewer notes it can clog pores and cause breakouts if not double-cleansed, and another felt it left pores clogged.
concerns.oiliness: Many reviewers, including several with oily skin, report a matte or non-greasy, non-oily finish; one oily-skin reviewer found the texture too thick and gunky.

extraits.texte: I found this to be greasy. I have dry skin and I would NEVER use this on my face--maybe as a moisturizer on my feet or hands.

extraits.titre: Great primer, sunscreen is just okay
extraits.texte: This is a great primer, and I love it as a primer! The sunscreen is just okay. As a primer, it blurs my pores and it works really well with my oily skin, and it doesn't get in my eyes when I sweat (going out for a run outside). As a sunscreen, it isn't enough protection for me (I reapplied after about an hour but I still got pink from the sun). Maybe I should have reapplied after 30 minutes, or maybe I shouldn't expect so much from only SPF 35. Either way, I love it as a primer but as a sunscreen it is ehh just okay...full disclosure I am a natural redhead/ginger and I probably really need SPF 50.

for the past 40 years, since I was maybe 25-30 I have tried many, many, many sunscreens specifically for the face. Every one (within my budget) was greasy,heavy, and always broke my face out in a spot or 2. So I typically do not use sunscreen on my face. Well I do now! I thought I'd give it a try and after using for 10 days, it's lightweight, makes my complexion look so smooth, no grease or oil and not one adverse reaction (breakout). I'm going to stock up just in case ELF discontinues this one. It's amazing for me.

extraits.titre: The best sunscreen ever for sensitive skin and doe
extraits.texte: This is the first sunscreen I have ever used that has not caused an allergic reaction on my skin. I have tried so many sunscreens over the years and every time I apply them my skin gets extremely red, swollen itchy, and irritated, but this went on very smooth, it actually minimize my pores and felt like a cool moisturizer rather than grease standing on top of it. I hate the oily feeling of sunscreens and this overall still made my skin feel like clean skin not gross. I will definitely be purchasing this in the future.

This product is a silicone based blurring primer first and a "sunscreen" second. It definitely blurs my pores as advertised, leaving the skin feeling silky smooth and has no fragrance. I'm unsure about using it as my only form of sun protection, since it's only spf 35 and you'd require a lot of product to cover the face. Since it's silicone based I find that this can clog the pores and break me out if not double cleansed properly. Other than that, this is a nice product to use daily for a bare face look but it also provides a nice base for makeup in general.

I have oily skin but this sunscreen blurs my pores and leaves me with a matte dewy look if that makes sense? It feels like a silicone primer and layers nicely with makeup. I wish they sold a larger size.

Deducted some points because this comes out super thick and I don't like the way it sits on my face. Would not recommend for oily skin. His a light scent which I appreciate but would not use this on the daily.
